test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

The engineers completed the structural analysis before the design phase began.

options.text: The structural analysis is completed by the engineers before the design phase began.
The structural analysis was being completed by the engineers before the design phase began.
The structural analysis had been completed by the engineers before the design phase began.
The structural analysis was completed by the engineers before the design phase began.

solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. The structural analysis was completed by the engineers before the design phase began..

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice**, where the subject "The engineers" performs the action "completed the structural analysis".
 
• To convert a sentence into the **passive voice**, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject, and the verb is changed to the passive form.
 
• The correct passive structure for the given sentence is **"was completed"**, as the action occurred in the past.

Correct sentence: *The structural analysis was completed by the engineers before the design phase began.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive Voice Rules:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Object + auxiliary verb (was/were) + past participle + by + subject.
 
• **Example:** Active: "The chef prepared the meal." → Passive: "The meal was prepared by the chef."
 
• **Usage: **Used when the focus is on the action or the recipient of the action rather than the doer.
 
 
 
• **Common Mistakes:**
 
 
• Confusing tenses in passive voice (e.g., using "is" instead of "was" for a past action).
 
• Incorrect placement of "by" and the original subject.
